archetypes.name: env-split-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan splits test overrides into two separate env vars (LAUNCH_REVIEW_SH for Codex vs LAUNCH_SH for Claude only); existing harnesses that set the old single-override to stub all launches will silently stop covering the Codex path after the split.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan introduces two distinct test-override env vars: `SCOUT_DYNAMIC_ARCHETYPES_LAUNCH_REVIEW_SH` for the Codex tier and `SCOUT_DYNAMIC_ARCHETYPES_LAUNCH_SH` exclusively for the Claude tier. Check whether every existing harness and caller that currently sets `SCOUT_DYNAMIC_ARCHETYPES_LAUNCH_SH` to stub all scout launches will silently stop intercepting the Codex path once the split takes effect, leaving Codex calls hitting real binaries during test runs. Verify that sibling .md contracts and test files document this API split clearly enough that a future contributor cannot accidentally use the wrong override variable for each tier. Look for any `dispatch-panel.sh`, `plan-review-loop.sh`, or wrapper fixture that sets the old env var and could now behave differently when `--codex-present true` is forwarded. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: status-state-machine
archetypes.rationale: The plan encodes a three-way terminal status split (parse-failed / empty / launcher-failure codes) with different rules for single-tier vs multi-tier exhaustion; missing or ambiguous transitions could silently suppress dispatch-panel diagnostics or fire them incorrectly.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan encodes three terminal outcomes from the waterfall: single-tier Claude-only exit-0 raw failing probe or validation emits `SCOUT_STATUS=parse-failed`; multi-tier exhaustion with at least one exit-0 tier that fails the probe emits `SCOUT_STATUS=empty`; every tier failing launch emits launcher-failure codes. Check for unspecified transitions — for example, when `--codex-present true` but Codex exits 0 with valid probe JSON and then downstream validation fails, should the terminal status be `parse-failed` or `empty`, and does the plan resolve this clearly. Verify that `dispatch-panel.sh` parse-failed diagnostics are not silently suppressed for the multi-tier path, and that the planned test cases for `SCOUT_FAIL_REASON` tokens (`missing-raw`, `malformed`, `invalid-shape`) explicitly test the single-tier Claude-only path rather than inadvertently running with `--codex-present true` where the same malformed raw would yield `empty` instead. Confirm the plan covers all loop exit paths so no code path can exit with an undeclared status value. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: staged-path-scope
archetypes.rationale: The plan stages context into $SESSION_ROOT/staged-context/ with stable basenames, but SESSION_ROOT may not be defined in all call contexts and concurrent scout calls within the same session could collide on those basenames.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan stages every bulk context file into `$SESSION_ROOT/staged-context/` with fixed basenames (`diff.txt`, `plan.txt`, etc.), but the plan body describes callers passing paths under `$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR`, `design-export/`, and other session-specific tmpdirs — check whether `SESSION_ROOT` is actually defined and exported in every call context (design plan-review-loop, implement dispatch-panel) or whether the plan conflates it with a different per-session variable. Look for whether concurrent scout invocations within the same session (e.g., two review rounds) could overwrite each other's staged files under the shared stable basenames before the earlier tier has finished reading them. Verify the plan addresses cleanup of staged files so they do not accumulate across rounds or persist into a subsequent session on the same host. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
